narrative.overview: Misul Agent is a private engineering workspace whose computer is the phone itself. Misul supplies the harmonic-arcs identity, editorial discipline, and cobalt energy; PhoneCode supplies the native transcript, local tools, explicit approvals, and durable state. The interface is brandful at the edges and quiet at the center: conversation first, proof over theater, and speed through restraint.
keyCharacteristics: Conversation is the primary surface, never a dashboard.
Soft-black and clean-white foundations with cobalt reserved for active agency.
System typography for daily work, Instrument Sans for rare brand moments, JetBrains Mono for machine material.
Tonal layering and fine rules instead of card grids and decorative shadows.
Fast, interruptible, frequency-aware motion with a complete reduced-motion path.
Local runtime, tools, approvals, recovery, and uncertainty remain inspectable.

rules.name: The Current Rule
rules.body: Cobalt means selected, focused, or actively working. It does not fill general navigation or permanent surfaces.

rules.name: The One Plane Rule
rules.body: Use tonal contrast, a rule, blur, or shadow to establish an edge, but rarely more than two together.

rules.name: The Frequency Gate
rules.body: High-frequency work receives no animation; occasional spatial changes receive fast purposeful motion; rare identity moments may carry restrained delight.

dos: Do make the transcript the first and dominant screen after setup.
Do use the canonical harmonic-arcs mark and reserve the luminous field for rare identity moments.
Do preserve exact tool provenance, consequences, failure states, and recovery choices.
Do keep every interactive target at least 48px and every gesture paired with a visible action.
Do validate the running app across themes, window sizes, accessibility settings, keyboard states, and local-runtime failures.
donts: Don't build a dashboard, control-center home, or grid of agent-status cards.
Don't turn the neutral canvas blue-black or spread cobalt across general chrome.
Don't keep a live shader behind the working transcript.
Don't wrap every response or tool event in decorative cards.
Don't animate typing, sending, streaming tokens, keyboard actions, or other high-frequency work.
Don't use vague destructive labels, fake progress, or completion claims without actual evidence.
